rules.title: RSO rent increases limited to once every 12 months by allowable percentage
rules.requirement: For rental units subject to the City of Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance, rent may be increased only once every 12 months and only by the allowable rent increase percentage published by LAHD, unless a listed exception applies or LAHD approves a further increase.
rules.citation: LAHD, RSO Overview (https://housing.lacity.gov/residents/rso-overview), 'When Can Rent Be Increased'
rules.quoted_span: Rent may be increased once every 12 months by the allowable rent increase percentage
rules.key_value: once every 12 months; allowable percentage per LAHD PDF (percentage not stated in this chunk)
rules.exemptions: Page states the RSO generally covers rental properties first built on or before October 1, 1978, plus replacement units under LAMC 151.28. Rent amount is not regulated for condominium and townhome tenancies that commenced after December 31, 1995. Rent may be raised to market rate if the tenant voluntarily moves out, is evicted for nonpayment or lease violation, is evicted for failure to comply with a Tenant Habitability Plan or per a City Attorney order, or accepts a Tenant Buyout Agreement. Additional increases are available through LAHD-approved programs (Capital Improvement, Primary Renovation, Seismic Retrofit, Rehabilitation, Just and Reasonable). A Luxury Exemption is available on application.
rules.interaction: Related to the Feb 2, 2026 changes removing the utilities percentage and the additional-dependent 10% increase. Coverage uses the city_rent_controlled fact because the page's coverage criteria (first built on or before Oct 1, 1978, property type, tenancy commencement date) cannot all be safely encoded with the allowed fields.

rules.title: No additional percentage rent increase for utilities (RSO)
rules.requirement: Effective February 2, 2026, landlords of RSO units can no longer include an additional percentage increase for utilities when increasing rent.
rules.citation: LAHD, RSO Overview (https://housing.lacity.gov/residents/rso-overview), 'When Can Rent Be Increased'
rules.quoted_span: Effective February 2, 2026, the landlord can no longer include an additional percentage increase for utilities.
rules.exemptions: Same RSO coverage limits as the annual increase rule; no separate exemptions stated.
rules.interaction: Modifies the allowable annual increase computation in la-rso-annual-rent-increase-once-per-12-months. The underlying ordinance or amendment number is not given in this chunk.

rules.title: No additional 10% increase for an added dependent (RSO)
rules.requirement: Effective February 2, 2026, landlords of RSO units may no longer impose an additional 10% rent increase for an additional dependent added to the tenancy. The page states a 10% increase for an additional non-dependent tenant remains allowed, within 60 days of learning of the tenant.
rules.citation: LAHD, RSO Overview (https://housing.lacity.gov/residents/rso-overview), 'When Can Rent Be Increased'
rules.quoted_span: Effective February 2, 2026, an additonal 10% increase for an additional dependent added to the tenancy is no longer permitted.
rules.exemptions: None stated; the 10% increase for an additional tenant who is not a dependent remains allowed per the page.

rules.title: RSO limits evictions to listed legal reasons
rules.requirement: The RSO covers legal reasons for eviction. The page lists at-fault reasons (failure to pay rent, uncured lease violation, nuisance or damage, illegal use, failure to renew a similar rental agreement, failure to provide reasonable access, unapproved subtenant at end of lease term) and no-fault reasons (owner or immediate family move-in, resident manager move-in, demolition and permanent removal from the rental market, government order, conversion to affordable housing).
rules.citation: LAHD, RSO Overview (https://housing.lacity.gov/residents/rso-overview), 'Legal Reasons for Eviction' (specific LAMC section not given in this chunk)
rules.interaction: The page separately says non-RSO properties still have rights and responsibilities under the Just Cause Ordinance; its terms are not in this chunk.

rules.title: Relocation assistance required for no-fault evictions (RSO)
rules.requirement: No-fault evictions of RSO units require payment of tenant relocation assistance. Landlords must file a Landlord Declaration of Intent to Evict with LAHD and give written notice (30-day and 60-day; some evictions require 120-day notice or up to a 1-year extension). Relocation amounts are not stated in this chunk.

rules.title: Eviction termination notices must be filed with LAHD within three business days
rules.requirement: All notices to terminate a tenancy for rental units subject to the RSO must be filed with LAHD within three business days of service on the tenant.
rules.citation: LAMC 151.09.C.9 & 165.05.B.5 (as cited by LAHD, RSO Overview)
rules.quoted_span: three (3) business days of service on the tenant
